name: Groom new issues
description: A maintainer opens an issue; om-auto-manage-issues adds SDLC labels, a Definition of Ready check and implementation notes (ADR 0017). `authors` is the gate: the run holds Bash with no allowlist, so an issue from anyone else is groomed only when a maintainer adds `groom`. Issues a run holds or a human put on hold never match.

name: Re-groom on request
description: A label only a collaborator can set: `groom` re-runs om-auto-manage-issues on one issue (an external report a maintainer vouches for, an edit, a reply). The override removes the label first.

name: Fix issues on the autofix label
description: A human adds `autofix`; om-auto-fix-issue drives the issue to a reviewed PR on develop (ADR 0017). Held, blocked, do-not-merge or spec-pending issues never match.

name: Write a spec for feature issues
description: A human adds `spec` to a `feature` issue; om-auto-write-spec lands .ai/specs/<date>-<slug>.md on a design-only PR (ADR 0017).

name: Autopilot new pull requests
description: A human maintainer opens a PR; om-pr-autopilot diagnoses and runs the right chain through to the merge into develop (ADR 0027). Agent PRs (authored by design4pro-agent, the cockpit's gh identity) and dependabot are excluded by author; pipeline labels exclude the race with om-open-pr. The standing develop-to-main promotion PR is opened with a maintainer's token - which makes `pull_request` workflows run on it - so the author filter cannot tell it apart from a hand-opened one, and no filter here reads the base branch. .github/workflows/promote-develop.yml therefore opens it carrying `merge-queue`, which `excludeLabels` already stands down on.

name: Merge reviewed agent pull requests
description: An agent PR (authored by design4pro-agent) that om-auto-review-pr approved into `merge-queue` gets om-pr-autopilot --allow-merge, which merges it into develop through om-approve-merge-pr (ADR 0027). The promotion PR is authored by a maintainer, so the author filter keeps it out.

name: Triage new issues
description: A human adds `needs-triage`; afk-triage verifies the report, writes an Agent Brief comment and sets exactly one intake label. The label is the gate - only a collaborator can set one - which is also why this does not fire on `issue.opened` the way it does in cezar: om-auto-manage-issues already owns that event here, and two autonomous runs grooming the same fresh issue would race on its labels. Groom first, then ask for a brief.

name: Implement ready-for-agent issues
description: An issue labeled `ready-for-agent` is implemented test-first in a worktree from its Agent Brief, gated, opened as a PR and reviewed. Never merges. Distinct from "Fix issues on the autofix label", which drives an ungroomed issue end to end - these two never contend for the same issue because they watch different labels. `risk-high` and `security` are not excluded: afk-triage promotes those to `ready-for-agent` only on the security and tenancy specialist's approving verdict (SDLC.md § Delegated decisions), and the PR is still never merged automatically. `allLabels: ["risk-low"]` narrows it further, so only low-risk work starts by itself: a `risk-medium` issue still earns a full Agent Brief and `ready-for-agent`, it just waits for a person to start it. Both groom and triage apply exactly one risk label when none is present, so an issue reaching this filter without one is a bug upstream, not a ticket this automation should guess at.

name: Spec to tickets
description: Weekday mornings: afk-to-tickets promotes the ticket frontier, then slices at most one newly merged spec into vertical tickets. Schedule rather than an event, so it never races the issue pipeline above: it reads `.ai/specs/` and the open tree, and only the frontier gets `ready-for-agent`. Idempotent - a spec that already has a parent issue is skipped.

task.prompt: Run the afk-to-tickets skill for {{project}} on {{date}}: promote the frontier, then slice at most one unsliced spec.

name: Weekly architecture review
description: Mondays: afk-architecture-review reads the last 30 days of hot spots and files at most three refactor issues, each with a recommendation strength. Read-only on code - the only writes are issues, and it never applies `ready-for-agent` itself: every candidate it files gets `needs-triage` so triage writes the brief, and a judgement call is settled by a specialist sub-agent (`.ai/skills/afk-decide/SKILL.md`). It reads `.ai/skills/afk-codebase-design/SKILL.md` for its vocabulary - the shared half, kept identical by hand across the repositories that use this pipeline - and this repository's own seams are in the override beside it.

task.prompt: Run the afk-architecture-review skill for {{project}} on {{date}}.

name: Weekly lessons
description: Fridays: afk-lessons turns mistakes repeated across the last 14 days of pull requests into enforced rules - mechanical ones into a lint rule, judgement into CODE_REVIEW.md, operational into AGENTS.md. A lesson seen only once is not a rule, so a quiet fortnight is a no-op, and it opens at most one pull request per run.

task.prompt: Run the afk-lessons skill for {{project}} on {{date}}.
